newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway premier reaffirms currency policy unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Norway premier reaffirms currency policy unchanged.

text.p: Prime Minister Thorbjoern Jagland reaffirmed on Friday that Norway's currency policy would remain unchanged despite the crown's strong rally.
Asked what to do with the crown, which climbed to a 52-month high at 3.9300 per mark in the afternoon, Jagland told Reuters: "That is the situation now, but we will see what happens."

Asked if Norway would abandon its policy of keeping a stable exchange rate, Jagland, at a meeting outside Oslo with fellow Nordic leaders, said: "No, it is handled by the central bank along the guidelines given by parliament."
Norway's central bank aims primarily at exchange rate stability. The bank intervenes in the market, but desired currency levels are not officially declared.

Finance Minister Jens Stoltenberg last Friday also said the policy would stay in place but he did not explain how the bank would dampen the rise of crown, which has firmed against European currencies despite three interest rate cuts in the past two months.
Announcing a 25 basis point cut in official rates last Friday, the central bank added it would now curb its fruitless intervention and let the crown run its course for a while.
